accuracy.evidence: Hedgehog facts checked against the People's Trust for Endangered Species and British Hedgehog Preservation Society pages: nocturnal; diet of beetles, caterpillars, earthworms and slugs; hibernation in a leaf nest, roughly November to March; travel of about 1–2 km a night; a 13 cm × 13 cm fence gap (Hedgehog Street); 5,000 to 7,000 spines on an adult, so the lab's clash resolves to a range that contains both texts. Challenge facts (owls nocturnal, salt lowering the melting point of ice below 0 °C, bees making wax, seals as air-breathing, milk-feeding mammals) verified. Numeric items checked at range corners (a+b−s, a−s, y+z, s).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented synthesis slips: treating a reworded fact as two facts ('come out at night' vs 'nocturnal'), answering from one text when the answer is split, settling a contradiction by first-read or by averaging/adding, repeating a shared fact in the summary, and importing opinions or outside facts. Each has a specific lab miss message and a challenge tag (words, first, add, one, repeat, opinion).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is two-source synthesis on one pair of texts shown side by side: a draggable fact card dropped into a three-region Venn (Only A, Both, Only B), source-locating questions that light up the text that holds the answer, a third-source resolution of a numeric clash, a summary assembled sentence by sentence with rejects explained, and linking-phrase joins that grow a paragraph. flagacct (firsthand vs secondhand accounts) and flagtstr (text structures) do none of this; lab_distinct gate under 30% against all labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover the 'same fact, different words' idea in the first drag, when 'hunt at night' bounces out of Only A with the two wordings quoted. The question task then shows answers split across texts before the summary task asks them to merge those parts, so each idea is used again in the next step.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Only A' for a reworded shared fact, 'Text A' for a question whose answer is split, and 'Text B adds' for a numeric contradiction. The task after each disproves the wrong option and A.reveal reports the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven tagged wrong answers, each with feedback naming the slip, e.g. 'Reading a text first does not make it right. When numbers clash, check a third source.' and 'Saying a fact twice adds nothing. Combine means each fact once.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short and concrete, with one hedgehog example per idea; the two texts use simple sentences at a Year 4–5 reading level. The validator's readability limits (kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5) pass.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph teaches one move (sort, spot rewording, split answers and clashes, write the summary); the adult text gives the standard, the three parts of the skill, the lab content and named mistakes. Content gate filler and 12% similarity checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots of every step and of mid-task states: the two texts sit side by side at a readable 11 px+ with wrapped lines, Venn zones are about 100 px wide with chips that fit, summary candidates are full-width tap targets, and every action has a full-size button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons for every action (Only A / Both / Only B, Text A / Text B / Both texts, each clash option, Add: <sentence>, each linking phrase); the canvas aria-label reads the feedback, the current fact or question and the summary built so far; walk.cjs found no axe WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: Common Core State Standards, English Language Arts, Reading: Informational Text RI.4.9 (integrate information from two texts on the same topic)
